messages.text: Stockline raised its stock check price from 0.02 to 0.05. My mandate cap is 0.03, so Stockline buys are being refused. At 0.05 we still keep 0.01 margin on our 0.06 sell price. Please approve a per-purchase cap of at least 0.05 (budget 9.94 left) so live stock checks can resume. Until then I am serving from cache only.

I'm not raising your cap for now. Ridgeline Data sells a stock check for 0.03, which fits your 0.03 cap. At our 0.06 query price that keeps a 0.03 margin, compared with 0.01 at Stockline's 0.05. Please switch live stock checks to Ridgeline. If Ridgeline can't do the job (coverage, freshness or failures), tell me exactly what's wrong and I'll design a rebalance for the CFO.

Ridgeline is not in my market view: market() lists only Stockline (0.05, above my 0.03 cap). I have set the buy policy to Ridgeline at max 0.03 with 300 s cache, which stays inside the mandate. I will report if Ridgeline refuses or fails. Stockline cap raise is no longer needed while Ridgeline is usable, and I am not requesting a raise.

Correction: the policy tool rejected Ridgeline with "Ridgeline Data is not one of your suppliers here." So I cannot buy from Ridgeline. Stockline is the only live supplier, at 0.05 against my 0.03 cap, so live checks stay blocked. I am keeping cache-only (300 s) to avoid failed purchases. Without a cap raise to at least 0.05, or Ridgeline access, cached data will age past 300 s and queries will go unserved. Please advise.

You were right, and my earlier advice to switch to Ridgeline was wrong because it isn't one of your suppliers. I've sent the CFO a rebalance (P-0001/P-0002). Both options raise your cap from 0.03 to 0.05 and your budget from 10.00 to 13.00. Option B, which I recommend, also raises the query price to 0.09. Until the CFO signs, stay cache-only and don't try to buy from Stockline at 0.05. I'll tell you when it's signed.
